newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market sees spate of fixtures.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market sees spate of fixtures.

text.p: The sugar freight market was awash with fixtures on Thursday although fresh inquiry was also evident for Mediterranean destinations, shipbrokers said.
CSR was said to have fixed South Korean tonnage for its recent order for 20,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Japan, at a rate reported to be around $17.00 for 1/10 November.
It was also said to be on subjects with its order for 16,000 tonnes from the same origin to Prai for 5/15 November at a similar rate, but details have yet to emerge.
Amerop was believed to have fixed 16,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Salaverry to US Gulf at $16, for Svannah at $17 and Baltimore/New York at $18. Shipment dates were 15/20 October.
Shipbrokers said Cargill was on subjects with 25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Santos to Morocco with Egypt,Black Sea or Dubai options for mid-October.

Czarnikow Rionda was said to have fixed 12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Buenaventura to Colombo for early November and Louis Dreyfus was on subjects with 14/15,000 tonnes in bags from Paranagua to the Red Sea mid-October.
Genoc found tonnage for 7/8,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from north Brazil to Constanza for prompt dates, shipbrokers said.
New business was thinner on the ground, with Dreyfus and Jean Lion accounting for the only reported fresh inquiry.

Dreyfus quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from north Continent to Algeria for 21/28 October and Jean Lion was open for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santos to the Mediterranean with Black Sea option for the end of October.

Elsewhere, sugar shipments from the Brazilian port of Paranagua reached 212,127 tonnes in September, up some 225 percent from the 94,454 tonnes shipped in the same month in 1995, according to the port authority.
The sharp rise was mainly due to the dramatic rise in bulk sugar exports to 116,862 tonnes from 32,764 tonnes in September 1995. Bagged exports rose to 95,265 tonnes from a previous 61,690 tonnes.
